script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. A LUXURIOUS PENTHOUSE - NIGHT

A dimly lit room filled with antique furniture, expensive artwork, and floor-to-ceiling windows revealing the bustling cityscape below. The sound of rain hitting the glass adds to the serene ambiance.

In the center, a man, JAMES (50s, impeccably dressed, with an air of sophistication), sits in a leather armchair, gazing at his reflection in the glass. He looks weary and haunted.

Suddenly, a knock echoes through the room.

JAMES
(to himself)
Who could that be?

He rises and approaches the door.

INT. ENTRANCE HALL - NIGHT

James opens the door to reveal a young woman, LUCY (30s, dressed in a simple yet elegant outfit, with a determined expression).

LUCY
(smiling)
Hello, Mr. Johnson. I've come to see you about a second chance.

JAMES
(surprised)
Miss... I'm not expecting anyone. Please, come in.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James offers Lucy a seat. She sits across from him, her eyes fixed on his.

LUCY
You may not remember me, but we met fifteen years ago. You were my professor back then, and you gave me an F on a paper that I had worked hard on. You said I lacked creativity and had no potential as a writer.

James looks thoughtful, recalling the memory.

JAMES
I remember now. Your story was clichéd and lacked depth. I was wrong to judge you so harshly.

Lucy nods, a small smile playing on her lips.

LUCY
I've been working on my craft ever since then. I've written countless stories, worked as an assistant to various writers, and finally, I believe I've found my voice.

James leans forward, intrigued.

JAMES
And now you want a second chance from me?

LUCY
Yes, Mr. Johnson. I want you to read my latest work and give me your honest opinion. I believe that, with your guidance, I can truly succeed this time.

INT. JAMES' STUDY - DAY

James sits at his desk, surrounded by books and papers. Lucy enters, carrying a folder.

LUCY
Here it is, Mr. Johnson.

James takes the folder, opening it carefully. He begins to read Lucy's story, his face reflecting various emotions as he absorbs the words.

INT. JAMES' STUDY - LATER

James looks up from the manuscript, a thoughtful expression on his face.

JAMES
This is a remarkable story, Lucy. It's raw, emotional, and deeply personal. Your characters are multi-dimensional, and your plot twists are unexpected yet believable. I'm impressed.

Lucy beams with pride.

LUCY
Thank you, Mr. Johnson. Your praise means the world to me.

JAMES
But there's room for improvement. You've shown promise, Lucy. With more practice and dedication, you can become a great writer.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James and Lucy sit in the living room, engaged in a heated discussion about her story and how it could be improved.

LUCY
(excitedly)
I've never felt so passionate about my writing before. I can't wait to revise it based on your feedback.

JAMES
(smiling)
That's the spirit, Lucy. You have a natural talent, and with hard work and determination, you can make your dreams come true.

INT. FADE OUT.

---

THE END
